name: ep24marco01
title: Start Where You Are
quote: Just start where you are, and trust the process.
detail: Marco shared that many people ask him why he doesn't expand his running club into other cities. His answer: connection takes time. You have to be there, to earn trust, to speak genuinely. He emphasized starting local, starting where you are. For Marco, that meant organizing themed runs in New York, like the popular 'Bagel Run,' and slowly building a community around shared values—movement, creativity, and connection. Proof Running grew not by chasing scale, but by deeply listening to people, offering real experiences, and staying consistent. His story reminds us that meaningful growth begins with presence.

name: ep24marco02
title: Proof Is Personal
quote: Your 'proof' is what you want to prove to yourself.
detail: When asked about the meaning behind the name 'Proof,' Marco explained it’s intentionally open. For one person, proof might mean completing a first marathon. For another, it's just showing up. The beauty, he said, is that each individual defines their own version of proof. It’s not about proving anything to others. It’s about honoring your own journey. His perspective reframed a word that might otherwise feel pressure-filled, turning it into something empowering and deeply personal.

name: ep24sunling01
title: Start Before You're Ready
quote: You don’t reflect and learn until you take action.
detail: Sunling shared a powerful metaphor inspired by educator Tao Xingzhi: 'Action is the grandfather, thought is the father, and creation is the grandson.' This shaped how she views creative process. Before any insight or outcome, there must be movement. When launching her Page One Workshop, she began not with a perfect plan, but by typing a prompt into ChatGPT. That tiny first step—taken before she felt fully ready—set everything in motion. The challenges came later, but so did growth. This story reminds us that action doesn’t follow clarity; it often precedes it.

name: ep24sunling02
title: Mess Is Part of Mastery
quote: Mastery looks like a loop, not a straight line.
detail: Reflecting on her Page One Workshop, Sunling admitted the process was messier than expected. Students struggled, tools broke, and she questioned her abilities. But a quote from NPR’s TED Radio Hour helped her reframe: 'You’re not regressing—you’re rehearsing something deeper.' That insight hit home. Learning, she realized, isn’t linear. It spirals. The confusion and setbacks weren’t failures but compost—fertile ground for future growth. Her honesty made the invisible parts of creative work visible, and deeply relatable.

name: ep24sab01
title: Run for Longevity
quote: Now I run not just for joy, but for a longer life.
detail: Sab shared her reflections after reading *Outlive*, a book about longevity. What changed her mindset was realizing how activities like running contribute not just to current well-being but to future health. She now sees running as protection—for her heart, brain, and mobility in later years. Inspired by the book’s focus on strength training and cardio, she integrated variety into her routine. This shift—from exercising to look good, to exercising to live well—felt like a quiet but powerful transformation.

name: ep24sab02
title: Don’t Compare Journeys
quote: I don’t want to prove myself to others. I run for myself.
detail: Sab raised a vulnerable but important point: the name 'Proof' initially made her uneasy. In many running groups, comparison is common—people collect marathon medals, share PRs, and subtly compete. She was reminded of the advice she often hears: don’t compare, just enjoy. But after hearing Marco’s take, she softened. Proof, she realized, could mean proving something only to yourself. That subtle shift—from proving to others to honoring your own path—opened a new, more compassionate way to frame growth.

name: ep24chen01
title: Every First Marathon Is Special
quote: Don’t chase perfection. Just enjoy your first race.
detail: Preparing for her first marathon, Chen admitted she was nervous—especially after injuring her knee. Marco reassured her: the first race is about experience, not performance. He shared a pacer's quote from NYC: 'If you trained, you’re happy. If you didn’t, you’re not.' His advice was clear—be conservative with pace, soak in the cheering crowds, and don’t let pressure steal the joy. It’s not about speed; it’s about showing up. Her courage to ask—and his encouragement—offered a reminder that beginnings deserve grace.

name: ep24mumu01
title: Weight Is Not the Goal
quote: The number on the scale doesn’t define your health.
detail: MuMu asked a heartfelt question about weight, muscle loss, and confusion over fitness. Marco responded with compassion: he hasn’t weighed himself in months. Why? Because health is more than numbers. Instead, he follows the 80/20 rule—eating well most of the time, allowing joy the rest—and focuses on energy, consistency, and balance. His point was clear: when we shift our focus from outcomes to habits, weight becomes a side effect, not a measure of success. Her question revealed a struggle many share; his answer offered a gentle reframe.

name: ep24harry01
title: Draw Your Line
quote: One day, you get tired of your own excuses.
detail: When Harry asked how to deal with laziness, Marco’s answer was honest and real: there comes a moment when you’re simply tired—tired of not starting, tired of excuses. He called it 'drawing a line in the sand.' Everyone’s moment is different, he said, but when it comes, you act. No hack or trick—just awareness and decision. This blunt but empowering message resonated. Sometimes, change doesn’t need more motivation—it needs truth.

name: ep24marco03
title: Create Something from Nothing
quote: I love taking something in my head and making it real.
detail: Marco described his joy of creating—from sketching a logo to designing a full brand. What excites him most isn’t just the outcome, but the moment something imaginary becomes visible. As a designer, runner, and community builder, he thrives in that space where ideas become form. Proof Running wasn’t born perfect—it grew through small steps and steady vision. His words remind us: creation begins when you believe your ideas are worth giving shape.
